summary: Bristol County, MA: a tower on Great Meadow Hill from 1916 until the Army had it moved to Long Hill in 1955; the Nike fire-control area built on the summit is now an Army Guard armory.

facts.design: Original steel tower (28-foot per the register, 50-foot per the former-site register) extended 12 feet after the 1916 move; 1931 replacement was a 68-foot steel tower with a 10-by-10-foot wooden cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed from Great Meadow Hill in June 1955 and rebuilt on Long Hill per the register; no source describes what remains on the summit

events.note: Register: a 28-foot tower stood on nearby Richmond Hill in 1912 (origin disputed; see resolved_conflicts)
Moved to Great Meadow Hill (register); former-site register says a 50-foot tower first operated in 1916 was moved here from Dighton, with a 12-foot extension and spiral stairs added
Land under the tower officially purchased; before this the tower stood on private land with the owner's permission
New 68-foot tower built to replace the older one
Commonwealth acquired about 140 acres and established Rehoboth State Forest; an existing fire tower was nearby on the summit of Great Meadow Hill
New cab and two-way radios added
U.S. Army ordered the tower removed for national security reasons; removed in June 1955
Register: reconstructed on Long Hill. Former-site register: moved about 3 miles south to Long Hill. State forest history: forced to Reservoir Avenue, Rehoboth (disputed)
Nike Battery PR-19 Integrated Fire Control area built at the top of Great Meadow Hill

corrections.why: Typo. The register gives Bristol County, Massachusetts for the Rehoboth tower entry; the former-site record also prints Britstol, which is a source typo.

resolved_conflicts.field: origin of the tower on Great Meadow Hill
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register: a 28-foot steel tower on nearby Richmond Hill in 1912, moved to Great Meadow Hill in 1916. Former-site register: a 50-foot steel tower, first operated in 1916, moved here from Dighton. Both agree it reached Great Meadow Hill in 1916; the height and origin differ. Not resolved.

Register: reconstructed on Long Hill. Former-site register: moved about three miles south to Long Hill. Mass.gov state forest history: a Nike fire-control area forced the tower to Reservoir Avenue, Rehoboth. Not resolved; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The standing Long Hill tower has its own record (data/research/us-ma-rehoboth.json). The Dighton record (us-ma-dighton) describes a Richmond Hill tower moved to Rehoboth in 1915 or 1916; reconcile the height and origin with this record. No visit report, access information, staffing or notable fire found for the Great Meadow Hill site. Mass.gov does not give public access for the Great Meadow Hill parcel, so no access fact is recorded. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook post about this tower did not load through fetch_text, so it is not cited.
